general-anaesthetics.moa: Enhance GABA-A inhibition and reduce excitatory transmission, giving loss of consciousness; ketamine blocks NMDA receptors; nitrous oxide and xenon are also NMDA antagonists
general-anaesthetics.uses: Induction (propofol, thiopentone, etomidate, ketamine) and maintenance (isoflurane, sevoflurane, desflurane, nitrous oxide) of general anaesthesia; ketamine for short procedures and in shock; propofol for ICU sedation
general-anaesthetics.adr: Respiratory and cardiovascular depression, hypotension, nausea and vomiting, hypothermia, malignant hyperthermia (halothane with succinylcholine); halothane: hepatitis; ketamine: emergence hallucinations; etomidate: adrenal suppression; propofol: pain on injection
general-anaesthetics.ci: Halothane: repeat exposure within 3 months and liver disease; thiopentone: acute porphyria and asthma; ketamine: raised ICP, hypertension and psychosis; nitrous oxide: pneumothorax and bowel obstruction; propofol: caution in egg or soy allergy

preanaesthetic-medication-drugs.moa: A group of drugs given before surgery: benzodiazepines (anxiolysis and amnesia), opioids (analgesia), anticholinergics (dry secretions, block vagal reflex), antiemetics, and H2 blockers, PPIs and antacids (reduce acid aspiration)
preanaesthetic-medication-drugs.uses: Reduce anxiety, pain, secretions, vomiting and the risk of aspiration; smoother induction and recovery
preanaesthetic-medication-drugs.adr: Respiratory depression, delayed recovery, dry mouth, tachycardia, nausea and urinary retention
preanaesthetic-medication-drugs.ci: Anticholinergics in glaucoma and tachycardia; opioids in raised intracranial pressure and respiratory disease; avoid heavy premedication in the elderly

sedative-hypnotic-drugs.moa: Benzodiazepines and Z-drugs increase the frequency of GABA-A channel opening; barbiturates increase the duration of opening (and open them directly at high dose); melatonin agonists act on MT receptors
sedative-hypnotic-drugs.uses: Insomnia, anxiety, preoperative sedation, seizures and status epilepticus, alcohol withdrawal and muscle spasm
sedative-hypnotic-drugs.adr: Daytime drowsiness, impaired memory, confusion in the elderly, falls, tolerance and dependence, withdrawal on stopping, respiratory depression with alcohol or opioids; barbiturates: enzyme induction and dangerous overdose
sedative-hypnotic-drugs.ci: Respiratory failure, sleep apnoea, myasthenia gravis, severe liver disease, pregnancy and lactation, driving, history of drug dependence; barbiturates in acute intermittent porphyria

antiepileptic-drugs.moa: Block sodium channels (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine, valproate), enhance GABA (benzodiazepines, phenobarbitone, vigabatrin, tiagabine, valproate), block T-type calcium channels (ethosuximide) or bind SV2A (levetiracetam); gabapentin and pregabalin act on the α2δ subunit of calcium channels
antiepileptic-drugs.uses: Generalised tonic-clonic and partial seizures; absence seizures (ethosuximide, valproate); status epilepticus (lorazepam, diazepam, phenytoin); also neuralgia (carbamazepine, gabapentin), bipolar disorder (valproate) and migraine prophylaxis
antiepileptic-drugs.adr: Drowsiness, ataxia, diplopia; phenytoin: gum hyperplasia, hirsutism, nystagmus, folate deficiency and teratogenicity; carbamazepine: rash, hyponatraemia and agranulocytosis; valproate: weight gain, tremor, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis and neural tube defects; lamotrigine: Stevens-Johnson syndrome; phenobarbitone: sedation and behaviour change
antiepileptic-drugs.ci: Valproate in pregnancy, liver disease and urea cycle disorders; carbamazepine in heart block and bone marrow depression; phenytoin in sinus bradycardia and heart block; many of these drugs induce liver enzymes and lower the effect of the pill and warfarin; never stop suddenly

antiparkinsonian-drugs.moa: Levodopa is converted to dopamine in the brain (carbidopa and benserazide stop its peripheral conversion); dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole, bromocriptine) stimulate D2 receptors; selegiline and rasagiline block MAO-B; entacapone blocks COMT; amantadine releases dopamine; anticholinergics (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) restore the dopamine and acetylcholine balance
antiparkinsonian-drugs.uses: Parkinson's disease; anticholinergics also for drug-induced parkinsonism; bromocriptine for hyperprolactinaemia
antiparkinsonian-drugs.adr: Levodopa: nausea, postural hypotension, dyskinesias, on-off phenomena and psychosis; dopamine agonists: sleep attacks, hallucinations and compulsive behaviour; anticholinergics: dry mouth, constipation and confusion
antiparkinsonian-drugs.ci: Levodopa: psychosis, angle-closure glaucoma, malignant melanoma and with non-selective MAO inhibitors; anticholinergics: glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy and tardive dyskinesia

antipsychotic-drugs.moa: Block dopamine D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway; atypical drugs also block 5-HT2A receptors and have weaker D2 block; many also block α1, H1 and muscarinic receptors
antipsychotic-drugs.uses: Schizophrenia, acute mania, psychotic depression, agitation, Tourette's syndrome (haloperidol), nausea and hiccups (chlorpromazine)
antipsychotic-drugs.adr: Extrapyramidal effects (acute dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia, tardive dyskinesia), hyperprolactinaemia, sedation, weight gain, diabetes, postural hypotension, QT prolongation, anticholinergic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome; clozapine: agranulocytosis, seizures and myocarditis
antipsychotic-drugs.ci: Parkinson's disease, coma and CNS depression, severe liver disease, prolonged QT, dementia in the elderly (raised mortality); clozapine in bone marrow disorders and uncontrolled epilepsy

drugs-for-mania-and-bipolar-disorder.moa: Lithium inhibits inositol phosphate recycling and GSK-3; valproate, carbamazepine and lamotrigine stabilise neuronal membranes and enhance GABA; atypical antipsychotics block D2 and 5-HT2A receptors
drugs-for-mania-and-bipolar-disorder.uses: Acute mania and long-term prevention of mania and depression in bipolar disorder
drugs-for-mania-and-bipolar-disorder.adr: Lithium: tremor, polyuria, thirst, weight gain, hypothyroidism, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and toxicity (vomiting, ataxia, coarse tremor, seizures); valproate and carbamazepine as for the antiepileptics
drugs-for-mania-and-bipolar-disorder.ci: Lithium: renal disease, pregnancy (Ebstein's anomaly), sodium depletion, and with diuretics, NSAIDs and ACE inhibitors that raise its level; needs plasma level monitoring (0.6 to 1.0 mEq/L)

hallucinogens.moa: Mostly serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonists (LSD, psilocybin, mescaline); ketamine and PCP block NMDA receptors; cannabinoids act on CB1 receptors
hallucinogens.uses: No accepted therapeutic use for LSD and similar drugs; ketamine is used in anaesthesia and for depression; cannabinoids (dronabinol, nabilone) for chemotherapy nausea and appetite
hallucinogens.adr: Hallucinations, distorted perception, anxiety, panic, flashbacks, psychosis; sympathetic stimulation; cannabis: red eyes, tachycardia, impaired memory and amotivational syndrome; PCP: violent behaviour
hallucinogens.ci: Psychiatric illness, pregnancy, driving and heart disease; abuse and legal restrictions apply

antidepressants.moa: Raise synaptic monoamines: SSRIs block serotonin reuptake; SNRIs block serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake; tricyclics block both reuptakes and also muscarinic, H1 and α1 receptors; MAO inhibitors stop their breakdown; mirtazapine blocks presynaptic α2 and 5-HT2/3 receptors; bupropion blocks dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake
antidepressants.uses: Major depression, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, bulimia, neuropathic pain, enuresis (imipramine) and smoking cessation (bupropion)
antidepressants.adr: SSRIs: nausea, sexual dysfunction, insomnia, hyponatraemia, bleeding, serotonin syndrome and discontinuation syndrome; TCAs: dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, sedation, weight gain, postural hypotension, arrhythmias, seizures and danger in overdose; MAOIs: hypertensive crisis with tyramine-rich foods
antidepressants.ci: MAOIs with SSRIs, TCAs, pethidine and tyramine-rich food; TCAs in recent MI, arrhythmias, glaucoma and prostatic hypertrophy; bupropion in seizures and eating disorders; watch for suicidal thinking in young people at the start of treatment

antianxiety-drugs.moa: Benzodiazepines enhance GABA-A action; buspirone is a partial 5-HT1A agonist; hydroxyzine blocks H1 receptors; propranolol blocks β receptors and reduces the physical symptoms
antianxiety-drugs.uses: Generalised anxiety, panic disorder and phobias (SSRIs are first line for long-term use), situational anxiety (propranolol), insomnia due to anxiety
antianxiety-drugs.adr: Benzodiazepines: sedation, ataxia, memory loss, dependence and withdrawal; buspirone: dizziness, nausea and headache; hydroxyzine: dry mouth and sedation
antianxiety-drugs.ci: Benzodiazepines: respiratory failure, sleep apnoea, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, substance abuse history and driving; buspirone with MAO inhibitors; propranolol in asthma

opioid-analgesics-and-antagonists.moa: Agonists act on μ (and κ, δ) receptors in the brain and spinal cord, reducing pain perception and transmission; partial agonists (buprenorphine) and mixed drugs (pentazocine) act partially; antagonists (naloxone, naltrexone) block the receptors
opioid-analgesics-and-antagonists.uses: Severe and cancer pain, myocardial infarction pain, acute pulmonary oedema, anaesthesia, cough (codeine), diarrhoea (loperamide, diphenoxylate), opioid dependence (methadone, buprenorphine); naloxone for overdose; naltrexone for alcohol and opioid dependence
opioid-analgesics-and-antagonists.adr: Respiratory depression, nausea and vomiting, constipation, sedation, miosis, urinary retention, biliary spasm, hypotension, histamine release, tolerance and dependence; pethidine: serotonin syndrome and convulsions from norpethidine; naloxone: triggers acute withdrawal
opioid-analgesics-and-antagonists.ci: Respiratory depression, head injury and raised ICP, acute asthma, undiagnosed acute abdomen, MAO inhibitors (pethidine), prostate enlargement, labour (foetal depression); buprenorphine or pentazocine in patients on pure agonists (precipitate withdrawal)

cns-stimulants.moa: Convulsants (strychnine, picrotoxin) block inhibitory glycine or GABA; analeptics (doxapram) stimulate the respiratory centre; psychostimulants (amphetamine, methylphenidate, modafinil, caffeine) increase dopamine and noradrenaline release or block their reuptake
cns-stimulants.uses: ADHD (methylphenidate, atomoxetine), narcolepsy (modafinil, amphetamine), neonatal apnoea (caffeine), respiratory stimulation in COPD (doxapram, rarely)
cns-stimulants.adr: Insomnia, anxiety, tremor, tachycardia, hypertension, loss of appetite, growth suppression in children, psychosis and dependence; convulsants cause seizures
cns-stimulants.ci: Hypertension, heart disease, hyperthyroidism, anxiety states, glaucoma, history of drug abuse and with MAO inhibitors; seizure disorders (analeptics)

cognition-enhancers.moa: Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine) raise brain acetylcholine; memantine blocks NMDA receptors and limits glutamate excitotoxicity; others (piracetam, ergoloid, ginkgo) have uncertain actions on cerebral metabolism
cognition-enhancers.uses: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (cholinesterase inhibitors) and moderate to severe disease (memantine); the benefit is modest and symptomatic
cognition-enhancers.adr: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, weight loss, bradycardia, syncope and vivid dreams; memantine: dizziness, headache and confusion
cognition-enhancers.ci: Cholinesterase inhibitors: bradycardia, heart block, asthma and peptic ulcer; memantine: seizures and severe renal impairment

antihypertensive-drugs.moa: Diuretics lower blood volume and peripheral resistance; ACE inhibitors stop angiotensin II formation and ARBs block AT1 receptors; sympathetic inhibitors (β-blockers, α-blockers, clonidine, methyldopa) lower sympathetic tone, cardiac output or vascular resistance
antihypertensive-drugs.uses: Essential hypertension; ACE inhibitors and ARBs also in heart failure, diabetic nephropathy and after MI; thiazides first line in many patients; methyldopa and labetalol in pregnancy
antihypertensive-drugs.adr: Diuretics: low potassium, hyponatraemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperglycaemia; ACE inhibitors: dry cough, angioedema, hyperkalaemia and first-dose hypotension; ARBs: hyperkalaemia (less cough); clonidine: dry mouth, sedation and rebound hypertension; methyldopa: sedation and haemolytic anaemia
antihypertensive-drugs.ci: ACE inhibitors and ARBs: pregnancy, bilateral renal artery stenosis, hyperkalaemia and a history of angioedema; thiazides: gout and severe renal failure; β-blockers: asthma and heart block; methyldopa: liver disease

antihypertensive-drugs-2.moa: Calcium channel blockers (amlodipine, nifedipine, verapamil, diltiazem) block L-type channels in vessels and heart; direct vasodilators (hydralazine, minoxidil, sodium nitroprusside) relax arterioles (nitroprusside also the veins)
antihypertensive-drugs-2.uses: Hypertension, angina and supraventricular arrhythmias (verapamil, diltiazem); hydralazine in pregnancy and heart failure; nitroprusside and labetalol in hypertensive emergencies; minoxidil in resistant hypertension
antihypertensive-drugs-2.adr: Dihydropyridines: ankle oedema, flushing, headache, reflex tachycardia and gum hyperplasia; verapamil: constipation and bradycardia; hydralazine: lupus-like syndrome and tachycardia; minoxidil: hirsutism and fluid retention; nitroprusside: cyanide toxicity
antihypertensive-drugs-2.ci: Verapamil and diltiazem: heart block, sick sinus syndrome, heart failure with low ejection fraction, and with β-blockers; short-acting nifedipine in acute coronary syndrome; hydralazine in SLE; minoxidil in phaeochromocytoma

some-combined-antihypertensive-formulati.moa: Fixed-dose tablets combine drugs with complementary actions, for example an ACE inhibitor or ARB with a diuretic or a calcium channel blocker, or a β-blocker with a diuretic
some-combined-antihypertensive-formulati.uses: Hypertension not controlled by one drug; fewer tablets help adherence
some-combined-antihypertensive-formulati.adr: The adverse effects of every component add up (for example cough with an ACE inhibitor, ankle oedema with amlodipine, low potassium with a thiazide)
some-combined-antihypertensive-formulati.ci: The contraindications of each component apply; avoid fixed combinations until the dose of each drug has been titrated; pregnancy for ACE inhibitor and ARB combinations

antianginal-drugs.moa: Nitrates release nitric oxide, dilating veins (less preload) and coronary arteries; β-blockers lower heart rate and contractility; calcium channel blockers dilate arteries and (verapamil, diltiazem) slow the heart; nicorandil opens K+ channels; ranolazine blocks the late sodium current; ivabradine slows the sinus node; trimetazidine shifts myocardial metabolism
antianginal-drugs.uses: Relief of acute angina (sublingual glyceryl trinitrate); prevention of attacks (long-acting nitrates, β-blockers, calcium channel blockers); unstable angina and acute heart failure (nitrates)
antianginal-drugs.adr: Nitrates: headache, flushing, postural hypotension, reflex tachycardia and tolerance; β-blockers: bradycardia and fatigue; calcium channel blockers: oedema and constipation; ivabradine: visual phosphenes; nicorandil: ulceration
antianginal-drugs.ci: Nitrates: with sildenafil-group drugs, severe anaemia, raised intracranial pressure, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and hypotension; β-blockers alone in variant angina; verapamil with β-blockers

drugs-for-peripheral-vascular-diseases.moa: Pentoxifylline improves blood flow by lowering viscosity; cilostazol inhibits PDE-3 (vasodilation and platelet inhibition); antiplatelet drugs (aspirin, clopidogrel) prevent thrombosis; vasodilators (prostaglandins, nifedipine, α-blockers) open vessels; antioxidants have limited evidence
drugs-for-peripheral-vascular-diseases.uses: Intermittent claudication, Raynaud's phenomenon, Buerger's disease and chronic limb ischaemia
drugs-for-peripheral-vascular-diseases.adr: Cilostazol: headache, diarrhoea and palpitations; pentoxifylline: nausea and dizziness; vasodilators: hypotension and flushing; antiplatelets: bleeding
drugs-for-peripheral-vascular-diseases.ci: Cilostazol in heart failure; antiplatelets in active bleeding; vasodilators in severe ischaemia with low BP (steal phenomenon); stopping smoking is essential

drugs-for-congestive-heart-failure.moa: Digoxin blocks Na+-K+ ATPase and raises intracellular calcium (positive inotropy, slows the AV node); ACE inhibitors, ARBs and sacubitril-valsartan lower preload and afterload; β-blockers (carvedilol, bisoprolol, metoprolol) reduce remodelling; diuretics relieve congestion; spironolactone and eplerenone block aldosterone; vasodilators (nitrates, hydralazine) unload the heart; ivabradine slows the rate; SGLT2 inhibitors improve outcomes
drugs-for-congestive-heart-failure.uses: Chronic and acute heart failure; digoxin also for atrial fibrillation; dobutamine and milrinone in acute decompensation
drugs-for-congestive-heart-failure.adr: Digoxin: nausea, vomiting, yellow vision, arrhythmias and heart block in overdose; ACE inhibitors: cough and hyperkalaemia; diuretics: electrolyte loss; β-blockers: worsening at initiation; spironolactone: gynaecomastia and hyperkalaemia
drugs-for-congestive-heart-failure.ci: Digoxin: heart block, hypokalaemia, WPW syndrome and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; start β-blockers only in stable patients; ACE inhibitors and spironolactone: hyperkalaemia and renal artery stenosis; avoid NSAIDs

antiarrhythmic-drugs.moa: Vaughan Williams classes: I block sodium channels (IA quinidine, procainamide, disopyramide; IB lidocaine, mexiletine, phenytoin; IC flecainide, propafenone); II β-blockers; III block potassium channels and prolong repolarisation (amiodarone, sotalol, dofetilide, ibutilide); IV calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem); others: adenosine (AV node), digoxin and magnesium
antiarrhythmic-drugs.uses: Supraventricular tachycardia (adenosine, verapamil); atrial fibrillation and flutter (β-blockers, amiodarone, digoxin, flecainide); ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation (lidocaine, amiodarone); arrhythmias of digoxin toxicity (phenytoin, lidocaine)
antiarrhythmic-drugs.adr: Pro-arrhythmia and QT prolongation (classes IA and III); heart block and bradycardia (II, IV); amiodarone: thyroid dysfunction, pulmonary fibrosis, corneal deposits, photosensitivity, liver injury and blue-grey skin; quinidine: cinchonism; procainamide: lupus; flecainide: increased mortality after MI; adenosine: chest tightness, flushing and brief asystole
antiarrhythmic-drugs.ci: Heart block and sick sinus syndrome (most); class IC after MI and in structural heart disease; verapamil in WPW with atrial fibrillation and with β-blockers; amiodarone in iodine allergy, thyroid disease and pregnancy; long QT
